answer: Incentives do the work here: a diverging juror loses stake only if the majority is confirmed by a second panel, which makes collusion expensive and honest dissent cheap. A duplicate submission forfeits the bond, and an idle identity bleeds standing until it is worth less than a new one. So a meadow of clones must stay active to stay valuable, and the timber of its stake keeps burning. The signal that gives it away is a shared funder.
